# Model card: research topic classifier (TF-IDF + Linear SVM)

*Generated by `python -m ml.model_card` from the result files. Do not edit by hand; re-run it instead.*

Component 3 (Research Intelligence & Collaboration Ecosystem), module 5: research trend analysis.

## 1. Model details

| | |
|---|---|
| Model | `TfidfVectorizer(ngram_range=(1,2), sublinear_tf, min_df=2, english stop words) + LinearSVC` |
| Run | `svm_tfidf_v1`, trained 2026-10-19T19:45:23+00:00 |
| Selected hyperparameter | clf__C = 1.0 (5-fold CV, macro-F1) |
| Input | Paper title + abstract, cleaned by `ml.text_utils.build_text` |
| Output | One of 5 arXiv categories: cs.CL, cs.CR, cs.CV, cs.DB, cs.RO |
| Training data | 8,000 papers (training split only) |
| Libraries | Python 3.12.10, scikit-learn 1.9.1, numpy 2.5.3 |

## 2. Intended use

- **Intended use:** suggest which of the five research areas a project title and abstract is closest to.
  The result gives context for the trend analysis (for example, "your proposal is closest to cs.RO;
  here is how cs.RO publishing has developed").
- **Not intended for:**
  - detecting research gaps or judging novelty;
  - assessing the quality of a proposal or a student;
  - any grading decision;
  - texts outside these five areas.
- **No "other" class.** The model always answers with one of the five categories, even for an unrelated
  text, so its output must be shown as "closest of five areas", never as a verified classification.

## 3. Training data

- **Source:** Cornell arXiv metadata snapshot (Kaggle), `arxiv-metadata-oai-snapshot.json`:
  - 3,215,335 records, 0 malformed;
  - SHA-256 `b7a2b3abd8fd6b3789307419f778741017d16f570ae44125e825e401f2eb9dab`.
- **Categories:** `cs.CV`, `cs.CL`, `cs.CR`, `cs.RO`, `cs.DB`. `cs.LG` and `cs.AI` are deliberately left out of this first version, because
  they are broad and heavily cross-listed.
- **Label:** Label = primary arXiv category = first entry of the 'categories' field. Only papers whose primary category is one of the selected categories are kept. Cross-listed papers are kept and labelled by their primary category.
- **Filters:** first submitted 2018–2024;
  abstracts of at least 30 words.
  - 114 papers were removed as too short.
  - 144 were removed as duplicate titles; every copy was dropped.
- **Sample:**
  - 10,000 papers, cs.CV: 2,000, cs.CL: 2,000, cs.CR: 2,000, cs.RO: 2,000, cs.DB: 2,000;
  - drawn by a seeded hash ranking, so it is reproducible (sample SHA-256 `4ff1d624ad77bf21…`).
- **Cross-listing:**
  - 48.6% of the sampled papers are cross-listed to some other category;
  - 7.5% are cross-listed to another of the five. These are
    the inherently ambiguous cases.

## 4. Evaluation protocol

Two evaluations use the same models, the same hyperparameter grids and the same test size.

1. **Random split.**
   - Stratified 80/20 split with seed 42:
     8,000 training papers and 2,000 test papers.
   - It measures performance on papers from the same period as the training data.
2. **Temporal split.**
   - Train on papers first submitted 2018–2022.
   - Test on papers from 2023–2024.
   - Sizes: 8,000 training papers and 2,000 test papers.
   - It measures how well the model carries over to newer research.

Leakage controls, applied to both:
- the split happens before any fitting;
- no paper id or normalised title appears in both train and test (checked, and the run stops if one does);
- TF-IDF is fitted inside the pipeline on training data only;
- hyperparameters are chosen by 5-fold CV on the training data only;
- each model scores the test set once.

Baselines go through the identical protocol: majority class, and TF-IDF + Multinomial Naive Bayes.

## 5. Results (held-out test sets)

| Model | Split | Accuracy | Macro precision | Macro recall | Macro-F1 | CV macro-F1 (train) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TF-IDF + Linear SVM | random | 0.9370 | 0.9373 | 0.9370 | 0.9371 | 0.9472 ± 0.0078 |
| TF-IDF + Linear SVM | temporal | 0.9285 | 0.9292 | 0.9285 | 0.9285 | 0.9498 ± 0.0036 |
| TF-IDF + Naive Bayes | random | 0.9320 | 0.9323 | 0.9320 | 0.9320 | 0.9339 ± 0.0048 |
| TF-IDF + Naive Bayes | temporal | 0.9085 | 0.9118 | 0.9085 | 0.9090 | 0.9397 ± 0.0060 |
| Majority class | random | 0.2000 | 0.0400 | 0.2000 | 0.0667 | n/a |
| Majority class | temporal | 0.2000 | 0.0400 | 0.2000 | 0.0667 | n/a |

### SVM compared with Naive Bayes

- **Random split:** the SVM's macro-F1 (0.9371) is higher than Naive Bayes (0.9320). On the same test papers, 53 were classified correctly only by the SVM and 43 only by Naive Bayes. This difference is **not** statistically significant (exact McNemar test, p = 0.358).
- **Temporal split:** the SVM's macro-F1 (0.9285) is higher than Naive Bayes (0.9090). On the same test papers, 79 were classified correctly only by the SVM and 39 only by Naive Bayes. This difference is statistically significant (exact McNemar test, p < 0.001).

### Effect of time

Moving from the random split to the temporal split changes macro-F1 as follows:
- SVM: 0.9371 → 0.9285, falls by 0.9 points.
- Naive Bayes: falls by 2.3 points.

Breakdown of the temporal test set by year:

| Test year | Papers | SVM accuracy | SVM macro-F1 | Naive Bayes macro-F1 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2023 | 865 | 0.9364 | 0.9361 | 0.9236 |
| 2024 | 1135 | 0.9225 | 0.9226 | 0.8979 |

The test papers within each year are not exactly balanced across categories, so the yearly figures are
indicative only.

## 6. Limitations

- **What the score measures.** It measures how well the model reproduces the authors' own choice of
  primary arXiv category among five fairly distinct areas. It is **not** a measure of research-gap
  detection, novelty or quality.
- **More categories will be harder.** Adding more, or closer, categories (for example `cs.LG` and `cs.AI`)
  is expected to lower the scores.
- **Labels are self-assigned.** Primary categories are chosen by the authors. Cross-listed and
  interdisciplinary papers have no single correct answer.
- **Language and source.** The model reads only English titles and abstracts from arXiv. Project proposals
  written in a different style may score differently, and this has not been measured.
- **Vocabulary drift.** Performance falls on later years (section 5). The model should be retrained
  periodically on newer papers.

## 7. Related output: historical trend analysis (descriptive, not a model)

`ml/trends.py` counts **all** papers in the snapshot (not the training sample). The snapshot ends on
2026-10-15, so 2025 is the last full year. Results are in `reports/trends/`
and figures 01–04 in `reports/figures/`.

| Category | Papers 2018 | Papers 2025 | Growth | Annual growth (CAGR) | Share of CS papers 2025 | Fastest-rising keywords |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| cs.CV | 7,261 | 27,877 | ×3.84 | 21.2% | 21.6% | diffusion models, large language models, vision-language models |
| cs.CL | 2,974 | 17,086 | ×5.75 | 28.4% | 13.3% | llms, prompting, retrieval-augmented generation |
| cs.CR | 1,530 | 5,799 | ×3.79 | 21.0% | 4.5% | large language models, prompt, jailbreak |
| cs.RO | 1,284 | 8,121 | ×6.33 | 30.1% | 6.3% | large language models, vision-language, diffusion |
| cs.DB | 377 | 969 | ×2.57 | 14.4% | 0.8% | large language models, text-to-sql, retrieval-augmented generation |

These are publication statistics. They show what is being published on arXiv. They do **not** forecast the
future, measure research quality, or identify research gaps.

## 8. Reproduce

```powershell
cd ml-service
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
python -m ml.prepare_data --input data/raw/arxiv-metadata-oai-snapshot.json --seed 42
python -m ml.train_classifier --data data/processed/sample.jsonl.gz --seed 42
python -m ml.temporal_eval --input data/raw/arxiv-metadata-oai-snapshot.json --seed 42
python -m ml.trends --input data/raw/arxiv-metadata-oai-snapshot.json
python -m ml.model_card
```
